g.name: GDPR (EU and EEA)
g.note: One regulation for all countries, plus national add-ons.

a.name: Own law, recognised by the EU as adequate
a.note: Data from the EU flows there without SCCs.

l.name: Own general data protection law
l.note: Transfers from the EU need SCCs and a risk assessment (TIA).

n.name: No general law found
n.note: None found as of June 2024; part of the list was rechecked on 17.11.2026.

united-states-of-america.law: laws of ~20 states, HIPAA, COPPA, GLBA

kazakhstan.law: Law on Personal Data and Their Protection

indonesia.law: Law No. 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection

argentina.law: Law No. 25.326 on Personal Data Protection

chile.law: Ley 21.719 (from 1.12.2026 by law, a delay is under debate; until then Ley 19.628)

dem-rep-congo.law: Digital Code, Ordinance-Law No. 23/010, Title III [data https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=CD&t=law]

greenland.law: Danish law for Greenland (outside the EU)

fr-s-antarctic-lands.law: French Data Protection Act (Loi Informatique et Libertés) applies [data https://www.cnil.fr/fr/comment-la-loi-informatique-et-libertes-sapplique-t-elle-loutre-mer]

el-salvador.law: Personal Data Protection Law, Legislative Decree No. 144 [data https://www.privacylaws.com/reports-gateway/articles/int195/int195elsalvador/]

guyana.law: Data Protection Act 2023, not yet in force [data https://www.mofo.com/privacy-library/guyana]

ecuador.law: Organic Law on Personal Data Protection

guinea.law: Law on Cybersecurity and Personal Data

gambia.law: Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025 [data https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-gambias-personal-data-protection-and-privacy-act-2025]

vanuatu.law: Data Protection and Privacy Act No. 13 of 2024 [data https://cert.gov.vu/images/legislation/Data_Protection_and_Privacy_Act_No13_of_2024-EN.pdf]

vietnam.law: Law on Personal Data Protection 91/2025, in force since 1.01.2026

mongolia.law: Law on Protection of Personal Information

tajikistan.law: Law on Protection of Personal Information

turkmenistan.law: Law on Information on Private Life

armenia.law: Law on Protection of Personal Data

albania.law: Law No. 9887 on Protection of Personal Data

new-caledonia.law: French Data Protection Act (Loi Informatique et Libertés) applies [data https://www.cnil.fr/fr/comment-la-loi-informatique-et-libertes-sapplique-t-elle-loutre-mer]

japan.law: Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI)

bosnia-and-herz.law: Law on the Protection of Personal Data

serbia.law: Law on the Protection of Personal Data

GDPR.s: The baseline model: six legal bases, special categories under Art. 9, breach notice within 72 hours, fines up to 4% of worldwide turnover [baseline 2026-11-17 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj]
d: Applies to companies in the EU and to anyone targeting or monitoring people in the EU (Art. 3).
A company outside the EU appoints a representative under Art. 27 unless a narrow exemption fits.
Age of digital consent 16, countries lower it to 13–15.
National add-ons: separate laws on cookies (ePrivacy), employee data, age of consent.
Transfers out of the EEA: adequacy decision, SCCs with a risk assessment, BCRs.
From 2.04.2027 cross-border cases get binding deadlines (Regulation 2025/2518).

Switzerland.s: Like GDPR, but processing is lawful even without a legal basis if the principles are respected. Fines up to CHF 250,000 on the responsible individual [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2022/491/en]
d: Sensitive data is wider: adds the intimate sphere and social assistance measures.
“High-risk profiling” and sensitive data based on consent need express consent (Art. 6(7)).
Breach: FDPIC “as soon as possible” when high risk is likely, no hour count.
Cookies: an opt-out model (Art. 45c Telecommunications Act), but EEA users get the EU standard.
The EU recognises Switzerland as adequate; to the US via the Swiss-US DPF.
Criminal fines under Art. 60–62 are prosecuted on complaint, under Art. 63 ex officio.

United Kingdom.s: UK GDPR plus the Data (Use and Access) Act changes from 2026: “recognised legitimate interests”, looser rules on automated decisions. EU adequacy renewed to 27.12.2031 [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=GB&t=law]
d: Age of digital consent 13.
A company outside the UK appoints a UK representative.
PECR fines (cookies, marketing) raised to UK GDPR level.

Since 5.02.2026 cookies used only for statistics or for appearance settings need no consent; the conditions are narrow [data https://ico.org.uk/media2/mufgyf25/mind-your-banners-the-icos-approach-to-sats.pdf].
Transfers from the UK: IDTA or the UK Addendum to SCCs; to the US via the UK Extension to the DPF.
Regulator: ICO.

United States of America.s: No general federal law. About 20 state laws on an opt-out model plus sectoral ones: HIPAA, COPPA, GLBA [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=US&t=law]
d: California (CCPA/CPRA): revenue threshold about USD 26.6M, or 100,000+ residents, or 50%+ of revenue from selling data.
A “Do Not Sell or Share” link and honouring the Global Privacy Control signal.
Several states require opt-in for sensitive data.
Fines are per violation, not a percentage of turnover; in California USD 2,663 / 7,988.
The FTC punishes deception in privacy policies (Section 5 FTC Act).
For the EU only companies certified under the Data Privacy Framework are adequate.

Brazil.s: LGPD is very close to GDPR: 10 legal bases, a mandatory DPO (encarregado), regulator ANPD [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=BR&t=law]
d: Breach: notify ANPD within 3 business days.
Fine up to 2% of revenue in Brazil, capped at BRL 50M per violation.
Legitimate interest exists, with stricter documentation requirements.
Transfers abroad: ANPD standard contractual clauses (2024).
EU adequacy decision of 26.01.2026: data from the EU flows without SCCs; Brazil recognises the EU in return. [data https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_229]
Children's data is processed “in their best interests”.

China.s: PIPL: no legitimate interest, separate consent for sensitive data and for transfers abroad, localisation for some operators [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=CN&t=law]
d: Data export: CAC security assessment, standard contract or certification.
Fines up to CNY 50M or 5% of revenue, plus personal fines for managers.
Data of children under 14 is sensitive.
An impact assessment is mandatory before sensitive processing and export.
A foreign company targeting people in China appoints a representative.

India.s: DPDP 2023: consent plus a narrow list of “legitimate uses”, no legitimate interest. Parental consent for everyone under 18 [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=IN&t=law]
d: Rules adopted 13.11.2025; consent managers from 13.11.2026; main duties from 13.05.2027.
No separate sensitive category: the same protection for all data.
A breach is notified to the Data Protection Board and to the people themselves.
Fines up to INR 250 crore (about 2.5 billion rupees) per violation.
Transfers abroad allowed everywhere except countries on a government blacklist.

Japan.s: APPI. Mutual adequacy with the EU, with supplementary rules for data received from the EU [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=JP&t=law]
d: Regulator: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC).
Disclosure to third parties by consent or under a registered opt-out regime.
“Special care-required” data: the equivalent of sensitive data.
Breach reporting mandatory since 2022.
Transfers abroad: consent with information about the country, or an equivalent protection system at the recipient.

South Korea.s: PIPA is one of the strictest laws, with a strong focus on consent. EU adequacy since 2021 [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=KR&t=law]
d: Regulator: PIPC.
Fines up to 3% of total revenue (2023 amendments) [data https://shinkim.com/eng/media/newsletter/2048].
Right to an explanation and to refuse automated decisions (since 2024).
Consent must be split by purpose more strictly than under GDPR.

Canada.s: PIPEDA for the private sector; Quebec's Law 25 is stricter and closer to GDPR. EU adequacy for commercial activity only [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=CA&t=law]
d: Built on “meaningful consent”.
Breaches are reported when there is a “real risk of significant harm”.
In Quebec: impact assessments, fines up to CAD 25M or 4% of turnover.
Federal reform: C-27 died; the new Bill C-36 was tabled in June 2026 and is still at second reading [data https://www.parl.ca/legisinfo/en/bill/45-1/C-36].
Alberta and British Columbia have their own private-sector laws.

Australia.s: Privacy Act 1988 and 13 APPs. Small businesses with turnover up to AUD 3M are largely exempt. No EU adequacy [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=AU&t=law]
d: Mandatory breach notification (NDB) to the OAIC and to people.

2024 amendments: a tort for serious invasions of privacy, tiered penalties [data https://nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/be98b0ff/australian-privacy-alert-parliament-passes-major-and-meaningful-privacy-law-reform].
Maximum penalty AUD 50M, 30% of turnover or three times the benefit.
The second reform tranche was published as a draft on 31.08.2026 [data https://www.wottonkearney.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Tranche-2-privacy-reforms-Wotton-Kearney.pdf].

Russia.s: 152-FZ. Russian citizens’ data must first be recorded on servers in Russia. The operator must notify Roskomnadzor before processing starts [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=RU&t=law]
d: Cross-border transfers must be notified in advance, to some countries only with Roskomnadzor permission.
Since 30.05.2025 a repeat leak brings a turnover fine of 1–3% of revenue [data https://seamless.legal/insights/Turnover_fines_and_criminal_liability/].
Consent to sensitive data in writing.

No EU adequacy; transfers from the EU need SCCs with a risk assessment that is hard in practice [inference https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection/adequacy-decisions_en].

Ukraine.s: A 2010 law. Bill No. 8153, close to GDPR, passed first reading on 20.11.2024 and is being prepared for the second [baseline 2026-11-17 https://itd.rada.gov.ua/billinfo/Bills/Card/40707]
d: Oversight currently sits with the Human Rights Commissioner.
Under the EU roadmap a National Commission for data protection should appear by the end of 2026.
No EU adequacy; transfers from the EU to a Ukrainian team need SCCs with a risk assessment.

Turkey.s: KVKK follows the old EU Directive. A 2024 reform of transfers introduced SCCs and BCRs [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=TR&t=law]
d: VERBIS controller registry (with thresholds).

Standard transfer contracts are notified to the regulator within 5 business days [data https://prighter.com/resources/laws/turkish-kvkk/by-laws/the-procedures-and-principles-for-the-transfer-of-personal-data-abroad/articles/article-14].
“Explicit consent” is read more strictly than under GDPR.
No EU adequacy.

South Africa.s: POPIA: 8 conditions for lawful processing, regulator: Information Regulator [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=ZA&t=law]
d: An information officer must be registered.
Breach: notify the regulator and people “as soon as reasonably possible”.
Some processing needs prior authorisation.
Fine up to ZAR 10M; prison is possible for some offences.

Singapore.s: PDPA: consent plus exceptions, legitimate interest since 2021. Breach notification mandatory [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=SG&t=law]
d: Regulator: PDPC.
Fine up to 10% of Singapore turnover or SGD 1M.
A DPO is mandatory.
A separate Do Not Call registry for marketing.

United Arab Emirates.s: Federal PDPL 2021. The DIFC and ADGM free zones have their own GDPR-style laws [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=AE&t=law]
d: The federal law’s executive regulations, which make its fines and procedures operative, are still not issued in 2026 [data https://www.businessdubai.ae/blogs/uae-pdpl-data-protection].
DIFC and ADGM have their own regulators and adequacy lists.
No EU adequacy.

Saudi Arabia.s: PDPL in force since 2023, penalties since September 2024. Strict rules on transfers abroad [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=SA&t=law]
d: Regulator: SDAIA.

Registration on the SDAIA platform is required for sensitive data or when processing is the core activity [data https://morganlewis.com/blogs/sourcingatmorganlewis/2024/12/saudi-arabias-personal-data-protection-law-a-guide-to-registering-as-a-data-controller].
Transfers abroad under the 2023 rules with a risk assessment.

Israel.s: Privacy Protection Law. EU adequacy. Amendment 13 (in force since 14.08.2025) widened the regulator’s powers and fines [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=IL&t=law]
d: Regulator: Privacy Protection Authority.
Database registration is now mostly needed only above 100,000 people [data https://www.pearlcohen.com/the-knesset-enacted-a-key-amendment-to-the-israeli-protection-of-privacy-law-summery-version/].

New Zealand.s: Privacy Act 2020, 13 information privacy principles. EU adequacy [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=NZ&t=law]
d: Mandatory notification of serious breaches.
Low fines (up to NZD 10,000) [data https://www.privacy.org.nz/about-us/opc-policies/prosecution-policy-2/].
Limits on transfers abroad (IPP 12).

Argentina.s: Law 25.326 (2000). EU adequacy since 2003. A GDPR-style reform is under discussion [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=AR&t=law]
d: Regulator: AAIP.
Databases are registered.
Argentina has ratified Convention 108+.
Regulator: URCDP.
Breach notification mandatory since 2020 (Decree 64/020), within 72 hours [data https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=UY&t=law].

Andorra.s: Qualified Law 29/2021 modelled on GDPR. EU adequacy [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.apda.ad/]
d: Regulator: APDA.

Mexico.s: A new federal law in force since 21.03.2025 replaced the 2010 law; the INAI regulator was abolished and its role passed to the Anti-Corruption and Good Government Secretariat [data https://www.legiscope.com/blog/lfpdppp-mexico-guia-cumplimiento.html]
d: A consent model with a privacy notice (aviso de privacidad).
No EU adequacy.

Nigeria.s: NDPA 2023 and the NDPC regulator. Controllers “of major importance” register and pay fees [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=NG&t=law]
d: GAID 2025: detailed implementing rules, in effect since 19.09.2025 [data https://privacymatters.dlapiper.com/2025/06/nigeria-ndpc-issues-gaid-key-compliance-insights/].
Fine up to 2% of annual revenue or NGN 10M.

Kazakhstan.s: A 2013 law with localisation: databases with citizens’ data are kept in Kazakhstan [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=KZ&t=law]
d: Breaches are notified to the competent authority.
No EU adequacy.

Indonesia.s: Data protection law 27/2022 fully in force since October 2024. Implementing rules (PP 33/2026) take effect 16.01.2027; the supervisory agency is not set up yet [data https://www.rsm.global/indonesia/sites/default/files/media/publications/Client%20Alert/2026/RSM%20Indonesia%20Client%20Alert%20-%20PP%20332026%20Six%20Implementation%20Priorities%20before%2016%20January%202027.pdf]
d: A GDPR-like model: legal bases, rights, DPO.
Fines up to 2% of annual revenue.

Thailand.s: PDPA 2019, fully in force since June 2022, regulator PDPC. A GDPR-like model [baseline 2026-11-17 https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?c=TH&t=law]
d: Breach notification within 72 hours.
Transfers abroad under 2023 rules (BCRs, SCCs).

Vietnam.s: Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025 in force since 1.01.2026, replacing Decree 13/2023 [data https://www.tilleke.com/insights/vietnams-new-personal-data-protection-law-a-closer-look/]
d: Impact assessments for processing and transfers abroad are filed with the Ministry of Public Security.
Fines up to 5% of revenue for unlawful transfers [data https://www.tilleke.com/insights/vietnams-new-personal-data-protection-law-a-closer-look/].

Chile.s: New law 21.719 (2024) on the GDPR model with a new data protection agency. By law it takes effect 1.12.2026; parliament is considering a delay to 15.10.2027 [data https://portalinnova.cl/proteccion-de-datos-personales-comision-de-la-camara-aprueba-postergar-la-entrada-en-vigencia-de-la-ley-21-719-hasta-octubre-de-2027/]
d: Fines will be revenue-based.
No EU adequacy.
